subject: CloudSpark bake-off: quality gates, owners, and test schedule
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kline <anna.k@cloudspark.ai>; eval@cloudspark.ai
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudSpark bake-off: quality gates, owners, and test schedule

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side. High level: CloudSpark is primarily evaluating for low-latency search reranking and multi-turn summarization workloads. We discussed performance vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints and Redwood’s differentiators around predictable tail latency, KV-caching for context-heavy workloads, and cost-per-token transparency.

Action items / proposed plan (owners + rough timeline):
- Deliver test plan and scoring rubric (attachment: redwood-bakeoff-testplan-v1.xlsx) — owner: me — by Tue 7/21
- Baseline hyperscaler runs (BigCloud + CloudGiant) on your dataset — owner: CloudSpark — complete by Fri 7/30
- Redwood run: 3 configs (default FP16, int8 quant, cached prefix path) — owner: Aditya Rao — run window Mon 8/2 - Wed 8/4
- Scoring and pass/fail gates: latency (p50/p95/p99), correctness (ROUGE/semantic match), cost per 1M tokens — owner: Vivek — report by Fri 8/6

Proposed quality gates (preliminary):
- P95 generation latency < 350ms for <=512 tokens (90% of queries)
- Semantic recall >= baseline hyperscaler within 3% absolute (on your eval set)
- End-to-end amortized cost advantage of >=20% vs hyperscaler configuration with comparable latency

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-testplan-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with tests), soc2-summary.pdf (security notes).

If this plan looks reasonable we can schedule the kickoff runbook sync on Wed or Thu next week and share the scoring doc. Please confirm owners and any additional data access requirements.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference


From: Anna Kline <anna.k@cloudspark.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: eval@cloudspark.ai
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudSpark bake-off: quality gates, owners, and test schedule

Thanks, Monica — all good summary and appreciate the detail. A few clarifying points from CloudSpark: 

1) Dataset & scoring: we will anonymize and provide a 10k query eval set + 200 longer multi-turn threads for summarization. Will the scoring rubric accept soft matches (semantic) or do you need exact-match checks?
2) Baseline hyperscaler configs: we will run BigCloud standard "c5-llm" endpoint and CloudGiant managed gpt-3.5-like SKU. We may also run a cached LLM setup internally.
3) Security: we need brief written confirmation that our eval traffic will not be used for model training and that logs can be turned off; we saw the SOC2 doc but would like a one-liner we can hand to procurement.

Tentative schedule OK. Please confirm: when you say "cached prefix path", do you mean Redwood will exercise your KV cache mode with warm prefixes identical to our production distribution? Also, what is your recommended load pattern for latency SLO verification (single-threaded p95 vs concurrent qps)?

We can do a 30-min kickoff Wed 7/22 at 10am PT or Thu 7/23 at 11am PT — whichever works.

Best,
Anna
Anna Kline
Head of ML Ops, CloudSpark
anna.k@cloudspark.ai


From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Anna Kline <anna.k@cloudspark.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudSpark bake-off: quality gates, owners, and test schedule

Hi all — quick technical answers to Anna's questions: 

- Scoring: we recommend semantic metrics (embedding cosine on chunked outputs + a small human-verified sample for calibrating thresholds). The attached scoring doc (bakeoff-scoring-criteria.md) has rubric examples; we'll accept both soft and exact-match buckets so results can be sliced.
- Cached prefix path: yes — we'll warm the KV cache with representative prefixes from your distribution before runs. We'll provide a warm-up period (configurable) and measure cold vs warm latency to show the delta.
- Load pattern: for latency SLO verification, run two regimes: single-request (p95 under a single simulated client) and concurrent burst (sustained QPS matching your production 95th percentile). For your case, propose: single-threaded ramp to 1 request/sec for 1k samples, and a concurrent test at 50 QPS sustained for 10 minutes. If you expect higher QPS, we can adjust.
- Security statement: Redwood does not use customer eval traffic for model training and can disable log retention for the run. I can draft the one-liner for procurement.

I'll own the Redwood runs (default FP16, int8 quant, cached path), plan to run initial baselines Aug 2-4. Monica — can you upload the eval set to our secured share or provide credentials so we can pull?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai


From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Kline <anna.k@cloudspark.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudSpark bake-off: quality gates, owners, and test schedule

Perfect — thanks Aditya and Anna. Confirming owners and next checkpoints: 

- Monica: upload eval set to secure share by Tue 7/21 EOD (I will also send a link to the onboarding S3 bucket)
- Aditya: Redwood runs (3 configs) Aug 2-4; please include cold vs warm cache measurements and attach raw logs + aggregated p50/p95/p99
- Vivek: scoring and cost analysis; deliverable Aug 6 with an executive one-pager highlighting pass/fail and recommendation

Kickoff: Wed 7/22 10:00 AM PT — invite sent (calendar link included). Agenda: quick runbook review (10m), data access & security checklist (10m), test matrix & owners (10m).

Quality gates update: we will treat the semantic recall criterion as the primary quality gate; latency and cost are pass/fail but we will present tradeoffs. If CloudSpark prefers, we can run an additional hyperscaler-config parity run (Aditya — please add a note in the spreadsheet about which hyper configs you want us to mirror).

Attachments: bakeoff-scoring-criteria.md (scoring rubric).

Monica
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
